source_evidence: an ETF’s market price may reflect a premium or a discount to the ETF’s underlying value or NAV
answer: An ETF’s market price can differ from its net asset value (NAV), which reflects the value of its underlying holdings. When the market price is above NAV, the ETF is trading at a premium; when it is below NAV, it is trading at a discount. As a result, you may pay more or less than NAV when buying shares, or receive more or less than NAV when selling them.
